extracted.intended_audience: mid‑career researchers (scientists, clinicians, healthcare workers) based at UK universities, medical schools, hospitals or research institutions applying for the Cancer Research UK Discovery Programme Foundation Award
extracted.subtask_short: CRUK Discovery Programme Foundation Award application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting outline and full applications to the Cancer Research UK Discovery Programme Foundation Award, covering eligibility, remit, application structure and formatting, required attachments, review criteria, costs and post‑award requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (core)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply if you’re a scientist, clinician or healthcare worker based in a UK university, medical school, hospital or research institution and can demonstrate that you meet the range of skills and experience as outlined in the ‘Transition to Scientific Leadership’ career stage in our competency framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must contact Cancer Research UK for an informal confidential discussion before submitting to confirm eligibility. During the full duration of the award you must be in a post that is fully funded by the relevant national Higher Education Funding Council, the NHS or equivalent. The award cannot be used to fund part of your salary. You should usually be a sole lead applicant; joint lead applicants may be considered if at a similar career stage and can demonstrate joint responsibility. You may apply toward the end of a CRUK fellowship or Career Establishment Award but cannot hold them concurrently. You cannot apply if you have previously held another large multi‑year award as an independent PI from another funder (exceptions may be considered—contact the committee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution must provide sufficient space and access to resources to undertake the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you receive core funding from one of CRUK’s institutes (including the Francis Crick Institute) you may not apply as lead or joint lead (you can be co‑investigator/collaborator). Institutional approval is not required at outline stage but is required online if invited to submit a full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible working and career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Career breaks, part‑time working and changes in discipline will be taken into consideration in assessment of outputs, achievements and career progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may apply on a part‑time or flexible basis if approved by your host institution. Contact the funder before applying to discuss proposed parameters and how to include part‑time requests in your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel and other funding disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit applications for the same research question to different funding bodies but may only accept one award if successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any parallel or other current and pending funding in your application under 'Other Funding'. Joint funding with other organisations may be considered—discuss with CRUK and the other funder before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme remit and suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports investigators who already have a salaried independent position to address an overarching question fundamental to cancer biology through an interrelated set of smaller questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal must present a well‑structured programme deliverable within the six‑year timeframe and, if building on prior work, explain how it develops and extends previous research. The committee supports work across levels (molecular to whole‑body), multidisciplinary research, novel technologies/methodologies (including imaging and radiotherapy), basic biology, disease‑specific research and preclinical studies generating biological data to underpin therapeutic development. Read CRUK research strategy for priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work not suitable for this scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will not consider applications that fall under other response mode committees or CRUK Horizons funding, including clinical trials, drug discovery as the sole function of the award, approaches in early detection or prevention, and pure technology development that does not aim to improve understanding of cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure which committee is most appropriate, contact CRUK for a recommendation or search other funding schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed based on scientific excellence, innovation and relevance to cancer research, considering alignment to CRUK's research strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Discovery Research Committee and Expert Review Panels evaluate scientific quality, novelty and relevance; more detail on criteria is available on committee pages. Success rates and historical data are provided (5‑year rolling success rate 25% for 2020–2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process and decision pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Express interest → outline application → committee consideration and written feedback → invitation to full application → Expert Review Panel interview → final decision by the Discovery Research Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are considered twice yearly. You must contact CRUK before submitting an expression of interest. Outline shortlisted will be invited to full and interview; committee takes Expert Panel recommendations into account. Timelines mean the process spans at least two rounds (minimum ~9 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and confidentiality / committee conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: CRUK will provide feedback on your application, but funding decisions are final and committee members cannot discuss decisions with applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not approach committee members directly. The Code of Practice for Funding Committees protects fairness. CRUK reserves the right to decline applications from anyone who compromises the integrity of the review process. Unsuccessful applicants may reapply after 18 months, subject to discussion with the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of panels (career development opportunity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early‑ to mid‑career researchers may be offered opportunities to observe panel and committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK prioritises offering observation opportunities to researchers from underrepresented groups. Find out more about eligibility and how to apply to observe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding period and maximum award
rubrics_metrics.description: Award duration: 6 years (or part‑time equivalent); funding amount up to £1.5 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding can be used to support staff, PhD students (stipend and fees), associated running costs and essential equipment. Specific exclusions and eligible cost rules are in the costs guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed and excluded costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible: postdoctoral researchers, technical staff, PhD students (stipend and fees), running costs, essential equipment. Exclusions: full‑time clinical fellows and infrastructure support that would otherwise be provided through clinical trials units, tissue banks or CRUK centres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide costs requested and justify them in the justification appendix. CRUK will apply indexation to costs and remove any ineligible costs; the final award may differ from requested amounts. Follow the detailed costs and salary guidance. For PhD students, CRUK pays a fixed sum and does not fund overseas fees or part‑fund studentships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline application format and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline research proposal: no template; general guide: number all pages; do not exceed 2,500 words (excluding refs, figures, figure legends, timelines, supporting roles and proposed level of support); single‑line spaced, Calibri 11pt, black; last name and initials in header/footer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available include preliminary data, figures and any unpublished findings or methodologies supporting the proposal. Figures should be in the main body of text. Datasets and preprints must be citable (e.g., DOI). Do not upload separate files such as unpublished manuscripts, ethical approval letters, patient information or preliminary data (they will be removed before review)—incorporate preliminary data into the proposal. Outline must include applicant info, career overview, skills and experience form, research abstract, research proposal and accompanying uploads per Additional Information list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application format and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Full research proposal: no template; general guide: do not exceed 7,000 words (excluding figures, figure legends and time charts); single‑line spaced, Calibri 11pt, black; number all pages; include last name and initials in header/footer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include preliminary data and figures in the main text; datasets and preprints must be citable. Do not upload unpublished manuscripts, ethical approval letters, patient information or preliminary data as separate files—they will be removed. Full application includes applicant info, career overview, skills and experience form, research abstract, research proposal and required uploads as listed in Additional Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline proposal: Purpose section
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly state the objectives of the proposed research and how these fit into the current research landscape, the significance of possible results and their relevance to cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At outline stage ensure context is pitched for experts in any cancer discipline; include why the research is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline proposal: Aims section
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overview of the key aims and how these interrelate to form a coherent programme of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how aims form a coherent programme rather than disjointed projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline proposal: Previous supporting work
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly outline prior work by you or others that supports the application, indicating how it was funded where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise referenced summary; if prior work is your own, indicate funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline proposal: Research plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe scientific methods and provide enough information to demonstrate why the approach will be successful and why you are the right person to carry out this work in an appropriate environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include methods, justification, and show feasibility for the timeframe. Indicate preliminary findings where available within the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline proposal: Expected outputs and future vision
rubrics_metrics.description: State the expected major outputs from the research and why they are important to CRUK, and include a description of your vision for future research stemming from this work and relationship with other funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For early‑stage translation proposals, share expected route to patient impact (not expected for all proposals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline proposal: Research team and proposed level of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Give details of the proposed research team, brief role descriptions and expected contributions; include the proposed level of support (staff numbers/types and approximate annual costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At outline stage you do not need to add team members in Flexi‑Grant, but provide proposed staff and ballpark costs. You don’t need detailed finances or AMRC full economic costing at outline, but preliminary costs must be a reasonably accurate indication of what you’ll request in a full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal: Research plan structured into work packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the research plan into work packages. For each package include the research question, experimental methods/analyses, any supporting unpublished findings or methodologies, associated staff, and expected major achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to your own published work or indicate availability of expertise where methods are specialised. Briefly describe expected major achievements per work package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal: Timescale, milestones and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a table of clear, well‑defined milestones and a schematic to outline timescales; list potential logistic or scientific problems and suggest solutions or alternative plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A realistic timescale and contingency plans strengthen feasibility assessment. Include schematic timelines and milestone table as part of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional documents and uploads (Required / Relevant items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include a variety of additional documents depending on outline/full stage: generative AI declaration, declaration of competing interests, cover letter (outline only, required for resubmission), reviewers, justification appendix, experimental design assistant report (where relevant), letters of support, data sharing plan, research declarations, costs, other funding, AMRC full economic costing (full application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Additional Information table for which items are required at outline vs full stage. Follow specific templates/guidance links provided for many items (e.g., conflicts of interest template, costs guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be asked to declare whether you have used any generative AI tools when completing the application form and confirm compliance with CRUK requirements on their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have used generative AI tools you must confirm compliance with CRUK policy and follow the instructions in the application form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: All lead and joint lead applicants must complete the provided conflicts of interest template in Flexi‑Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the template provided and follow the completion instructions in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter may be included with your first application (outline only). If resubmitting you must include a cover letter describing why you’re applying and how you addressed previous feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letters should be no more than one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer nomination and exclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You may nominate up to 10 reviewers qualified to assess your application but must not nominate individuals with close collaborations or with whom you have published in the last three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may also nominate referees to exclude from review with justification. CRUK will make the final selection of reviewers and nominations must comply with the conflicts of interest policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and industrial collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: CRUK encourages academic–industry collaboration. Most UK host institutions have technology transfer agreements; if not, CRUK standard terms apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal agreement is not required to apply, but you must provide a letter of support from the industrial partner describing nature of collaboration and contribution (funding and/or in‑kind). If awarded, share an outline of the agreement with Cancer Research Horizons before receiving funds; contact the Horizons team for confidential IP/technology transfer discussion before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research: sex inclusion and experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications involving animal work, CRUK requires male and female sexes to be used in experiment design unless a strong scientific justification for single‑sex experiments is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be granted with sound scientific rationale. CRUK encourages use of the NC3Rs Experimental Design Assistant (EDA) and requests submission of the EDA report as an upload in the justification appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A justification appendix is required for this award; it contains key supporting information such as experimental design assistant reports where relevant and cost justifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate guidance for completing the justification appendix (link provided in the guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support (full application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full applications must upload letters of support on headed paper from host institutions for any joint lead applicants or co‑investigators at different institutions, and collaborator letters of support describing expertise/contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborator letters should be a maximum of two pages each and must outline what specific expertise and skills they will contribute to the programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing plan (requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A data sharing plan is required to ensure data generated will be made as widely and freely available as possible consistent with patient privacy, IP and applicable law, and to describe how FAIR principles will be adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe when/how raw, processed and analysed data will be made available; provide ethics and patient consent statements for sharing (including withdrawal and de‑identified data); explain approach to sharing with commercial entities; detail processes and contractual agreements for international data sharing; list data standards/definitions to be used and alignment with community standards; describe data governance and architecture (include diagrams), and future ambitions/processes for granting broader access and infrastructure/timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research declarations and regulatory approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be asked about planned animal, human or human stem cell research and whether appropriate approvals have been granted; whether the work may produce outputs translatable to patient benefit or commercialised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International collaborations involving in vivo studies may require additional peer review steps to ensure animal studies meet UK ethical standards. If involving patients/tissue/info, secure ethical approval; CRUK and your host institution are responsible for legal and ethical compliance. CRUK can make provisional offers but funds may not be released until written confirmation of approval; factor this into proposed start dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs justification and AMRC full economic costing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide the costs requested and justify them in the justification appendix; as an AMRC member CRUK requires full economic costing information as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the AMRC full economic costing information form: enter total full economic cost of proposed research and the charity contribution requested. Note that AMRC info will not be reviewed as part of the final application; CRUK applies indexation and may remove ineligible costs. Discuss major equipment requests with CRUK before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑clinical PhD student funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: CRUK provides a fixed sum for PhD studentships; they must be fully funded for four years which must fall within the duration of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For standard Discovery Programme Foundation Award (60 months) you must recruit PhD students in the first or second year. If requesting a PhD student include this as a running expense in year one (one total cost) and do not break down stipend vs consumables. CRUK does not pay overseas fees or part‑fund studentships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment cost rules
rubrics_metrics.description: List all equipment costs requested for the full award duration and identify the 'claim year' (year first purchased/used). Equipment costs under £5k should be included as running expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If equipment is only required in later years (years 2–5) note this in the costs summary and provide details in the justification appendix. Requests for further equipment after initial application will not be considered in subsequent years of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other funding disclosure and fit with existing awards
rubrics_metrics.description: List all non‑CRUK current and pending research applications or awards (title, dates, amount, funding body, award type, current/pending) and explain how this application fits with any current awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps the committee assess time commitment and scientific overlap. Parallel funding applications are permitted but must be highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities within applicant team
rubrics_metrics.description: One primary investigator must be the named lead applicant who assumes responsibility for completing and submitting the application on Flexi‑Grant; team may include joint lead applicants, co‑investigators, named research staff, collaborators and optionally an administrative support contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead applicant must demonstrate ability to lead the proposal and be engaged for award duration. Joint lead applicants must be added as supporting roles once application is opened and will be recognised with equal status. Co‑investigators (not postdocs funded by the grant) provide major scientific contributions and may lead aspects of the project. Named research staff include funded postdocs. Collaborators (not participants on Flexi‑Grant) should be described in the proposal and justification appendix and in letters of support. Administrative support contact assists with submission and AMRC sections but does not need to provide a CV. For full applications, lead/joint leads and co‑investigators must provide up‑to‑date CV and five‑year publication history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and research outputs guidance (DORA and formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: CRUK is a DORA signatory and recognises a full range of research outputs. You may include peer‑reviewed publications as background and other outputs to evidence environment/network and efforts towards patient impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listing publications include a full author list; for very large consortium papers you may list first 12 authors followed by 'et al.' provided you denote your place in the author list (e.g., [Bloggs J, 15th of 65 authors]). Include publication title, journal, year and volume/page or DOI. You may include up to 20 of your most recent publications. List peer‑reviewed and non‑peer‑reviewed outputs in separate sections. Include other outputs (preprints, training delivered, consortia contributions, patents, datasets, software, novel assays/reagents). Research outputs must be clearly labelled and in a citable format (e.g., DOI). ORCID does not pull through author lists so enter manually if using ORCID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Flexi‑Grant system
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications (outline and full) are submitted and managed through CRUK's online grants management system, Flexi‑Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead applicant is responsible for submitting on Flexi‑Grant. If successful, you will manage the grant via Flexi‑Grant. Follow system guidance and invite required supporting roles when asked.
